title: Composable Tenant IaC plugin patterns for per-customer VPC extensions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: Customers frequently ask for small per-tenant network or service customizations (eg. VPC peering policies, custom NAT routing, additional bastion jumps, or private logging endpoints). Building a unique fork per customer is unmaintainable. We need an IaC pattern that lets us ship a single base module while enabling safe, testable customer extensions that: 1) avoid forking core modules, 2) allow upgrades to core modules without manual merges, 3) enforce policy constraints and drift detection, and 4) integrate per-tenant health checks and post-upgrade smoke tests.

Proposed approach summary: introduce a lightweight "plugin" or "mixin" composition layer around core tenant modules. The pattern has three parts: (A) core modules (immutable API surface, versioned with clear compatibility matrix), (B) plugin wrappers (thin modules living in customer repos that declare optional hooks and variables, and call core modules with sanitized inputs), and (C) a CI-driven validation layer (static variable validation, plan diffs gating, runtime smoke tests and health-check registration). Key design points below.

Design details (high-level):
- Module factory pattern: publish a single core module terraform/redwood/tenant_core with a small stable interface. Expose extension points as explicit variables of type object(map) and a limited lifecycle hook set (pre_create, post_create, pre_update, post_update) represented as lists of allowed actions (eg. attach_security_groups, create_peer, register_route). Avoid dynamic eval or template rendering inside core.
- Plugin wrapper modules: customer-specific repos include modules/tenant_plugin that compose tenant_core and add resources. Plugins must declare a compatibility tag (core_module_version range). Plugins are thin and must not mutate core resources directly; they attach using explicit outputs/inputs (eg. core.subnets_ids -> plugin.security_group_attachments).
- Variable shadowing and shaping: use a dedicated variable called extension_vars with a documented schema. Plugin maintainers can only add top-level keys that the core module exposes for extension. Use a schema validator script (python/terraform validate + custom JSONSchema) run in CI to fail fast on shape drift.
- Upgrade safety: maintain a compatibility matrix file in the core repo (compatibility.yaml). During core upgrades, run an automated upgrade-check job that runs the plugin CI against a canary core version in a staging workspace. If plugin CI fails, auto-open PRs in impacted customer-plugin repos with suggested fixes (generated by a linter) and block rollout until approvals.
- Health & post-upgrade checks: include a standard outputs/health_check_endpoint from tenant_core. Plugin modules can register additional checks by listing endpoints or k8s probes in extension_vars. The CI pipeline runs post-apply smoke tests in a disposable workspace and reports to Console rollout dashboards.
- Least-privilege and policy guardrails: enforce provider and resource policies via Sentinel/OPA or a policy-as-code step in the pipeline. Provider versions and lockfiles are audited; providers pinned in core modules and validated in plugin CI.

Operational patterns and examples:
- Example 1 (customer wants private logging endpoint): plugin declares extension_vars.logging_endpoint and uses core.network_endpoints output to create a route + security rule. No core changes required.
- Example 2 (customer needs extra NATs in specific AZs): plugin reads core.subnet_map output and creates extra NAT resources using a documented API; plugin CI ensures any change in core.subnet_map shape is validated.

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Stabilize tenant_core API and publish compatibility matrix. (owner: infra-module-team)
2) Implement schema validator and publish a starter plugin template repo (owner: platform-templates)
3) Pilot with 2 existing private customers (one small, one complex) using feature-flagged staging workspaces. (owner: solutions-eng)
4) Iterate on CI feedback, codify common plugin helpers into a small shared helpers module.
5) Roll out as preferred pattern + deprecate previous forked-iac playbook after 2 months of stability.

Acceptance criteria:
- Starter plugin template repo exists and passes CI against tenant_core@v1.0.0.
- Compatibility matrix and upgrade-check pipeline implemented and run in staging.
- Two customer pilots completed with documented runbooks and incident retros.
- Console shows health-check registration and pass/fail for plugin smoke tests.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Plugins could subvert core assumptions. Mitigation: restrict extension API surface, run automated shape validation, and enforce policy checks in CI.
- Risk: Upgrade churn for many plugins. Mitigation: automated compatibility test runs and bot PRs with suggested fixes; scheduled windows for bulk upgrades.
